history.summary: Coordinates (25.026192, 85.414452) are from a web place listing for this temple, not the map geocoder (rate-limited); treat as web-corroborated, not field-verified. The Lakshmi Narayan Temple at Rajgir (Nalanda district, pin 803116) is a pink-painted shrine devoted to Lord Vishnu and his consort Goddess Lakshmi, standing beside the Saptadhara, a group of seven hot springs. In ancient times the springs were the site of Tapodarama, a Buddhist monastery at the time of Gautama Buddha, and King Bimbisara is said to have bathed there. In recent times the spring has been tapped through ceramic pipes into a raised bathing hall where pilgrims bathe (Muslims are barred from the hot-spring bath hall per the consulted source). No consulted source gives a construction date or patron, so the temple's antiquity is unverified. Nearby: Vishwa Shanti Stupa, Ajatashatru Fort, Venuvana. Media note: the image in this file shows the Rajgir hot-springs complex where the temple stands; a photo of the temple building itself was not found in image search.

name: Lakshmi Narayan Temple, Rajgir
town_description: Rajgir, in Nalanda district of Bihar, was the ancient capital of the Magadha kingdom and is a major pilgrimage centre for Hindus, Buddhists and Jains alike. Set among five rocky hills lined with ancient cyclopean walls, it is associated with Buddha and Mahavira as well as the Mahabharata, and is famed for its hot springs, the Vishwa Shanti Stupa and the ruins of Nalanda, 12 km away.

travel.airport: Gaya airport, about 68 km away; Patna airport, about 98 km northwest (verify).
travel.railway: Rajgir railway station is less than 1 km from the town; Gaya junction is about 60 km southwest.
travel.road: Well-developed roads connect Rajgir to Patna (BSTDC round trips), Nalanda (12 km), Gaya (78 km) and Pawapuri (38 km); taxis and vans for hire from Patna.
